name: design-taste-frontend
what_it_does: Designs and builds a new web page from scratch with a deliberate look: it reads your brief, states the style it is aiming at, then writes the code.
what_you_say: build me a landing page for this that doesn't look like every other AI site
what_you_get: A one-line statement of the design it read from your brief, then the page's code written into your project.
on_your_computer: Writes web code (HTML, CSS, Tailwind, React) into your project and reads your project's `package.json`. If a package is missing it prints an install command for you to run rather than running it.

name: emil-design-eng
what_it_does: Reviews how an interface feels, and decides whether and how to animate something, using one design engineer's published rules about timing, easing and small details.
what_you_say: why does this dropdown feel off?
what_you_get: A before-and-after table of each change with the reason for it, and the CSS or JavaScript that makes it.
on_your_computer: Writes the animation and style code you asked for into your own files. Its fixed first reply prints a link to an outside course website as text; it fetches nothing.

name: frontend-design
what_it_does: Sets a design direction before the code: a small set of named colors, two or three typefaces, a layout idea, and one element the page is remembered by.
what_you_say: help me pick a palette and typography for this page
what_you_get: A short written plan with named colors and typefaces, a rough layout sketch, then the page built to that plan.
on_your_computer: Writes the page or component you asked for into your project. It reads nothing else and goes online for nothing.

name: image-taste-frontend
what_it_does: Settles the look in pictures before any code: one reference image per section of the page, read as the specification, then built to match.
what_you_say: design this landing page visually first, then build it
what_you_get: One labelled image per section, a written reading of each for type, spacing, color and components, then the code.
on_your_computer: Calls an image-generation tool if your Claude Code has one connected, once per section and often eight or more times, then writes the page's code into your project.

name: minimalist-ui
what_it_does: Builds a page in one specific quiet style: warm off-white background, strong typography, thin borders, flat grid boxes, pale accent colors, almost no shadow.
what_you_say: make this look clean and minimal, like Notion or Linear
what_you_get: The page's code, using this style's fixed palette, type sizes and spacing rules.
on_your_computer: Writes styled web code into your project. Where it has no real photograph it points the page at picsum.photos, a public placeholder service your browser loads from when the page is viewed.

name: mobile-taste-frontend
what_it_does: Designs a whole set of phone app screens that hold together: one platform, one navigation model, safe areas respected, each screen in its place in the flow.
what_you_say: design the screens for my app: welcome, home, profile and settings
what_you_get: The screen list stated up front, then each screen as a labelled mockup or as a written screen spec.
on_your_computer: Calls an image-generation tool if one is connected, several times in a session. It does not write app source code (SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose or React Native), by its own rule.

name: redesign-existing-projects
what_it_does: Goes through a site that is already built, lists the generic patterns in it across typography, color, spacing and missing states, and fixes them in the code that is there.
what_you_say: my site works but looks generic, upgrade it without rewriting it
what_you_get: A list of what it found, then edits applied to your existing style and component files.
on_your_computer: Reads your project's code and edits it in place. It checks `package.json` before importing a new library and does not run an installer itself.

name: frontend-surface-builder
what_it_does: Builds one page or panel inside a file list it was given, then opens it, screenshots it and reads the browser's error log before saying it is done.
what_you_say: build these three panels in parallel, one builder each
what_you_get: The files it changed, a screenshot, the browser's error output, and any shared file it needs someone else to change.
on_your_computer: Writes only inside the files it was handed, and opens the result in a browser window to check it. Shared files, such as page lists and site-wide stylesheets, it reports back instead of editing.
